subject: MAP: Eval environment gating — API keys, org access, IP allowlist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Montgomery <lisa.montgomery@edgecloud.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: MAP: Eval environment gating — API keys, org access, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Hi Lisa / Tom,

Following up on our MAP call this morning — attaching a lightweight checklist (MAP_checklist_v1.xlsx) so we can gate the evaluation environment quickly. High-level asks for the POC environment we need to complete within the next two weeks:

- Org & API access: please confirm the email(s) to be set as Org Admins in Redwood and whether you want us to generate a temporary API key or for EdgeCloud to create one and send it over a secure link.
- IP allowlist: provide the CIDR blocks your security team will require us to add (management plane + test agents). We need both the static ranges and an expected change window if they rotate.
- VPC peering: we need an initial VPC CIDR, preferred peering mechanism (AWS VPC peering vs Transit Gateway), and a contact for the networking ticket on your side.
- Timing: target timeline below — please confirm feasibility.

MAP milestone (proposed)
- Day 0 (today): confirm org admins + procurement owner
- Day 2: API key provisioning + IP ranges provided
- Day 4–5: VPC peering request filed and accepted
- Day 7: smoke test (canary workload, 100 concurrent sessions)
- Day 14: evaluation cutover and performance validation

If anything here is blocking on your procurement or security review, call it out and we’ll adjust the MAP. We can also do the VPC peering as a last-mile step if your networking team needs a longer lead time — we’ll run everything over the public allowlist first to avoid a hard stop.

Attachments: MAP_checklist_v1.xlsx (checklist), redwood-temp-key-approach.md (instructions)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Steph and Vivek for the peering/ops handoff once we have the IP ranges.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0183

--
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.ai
From: Lisa Montgomery <lisa.montgomery@edgecloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@edgecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Eval environment gating — API keys, org access, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Diego — thanks for the clear checklist. Quick answers from our side:

- Org admins: lisa.montgomery@edgecloud.com and tom.reed@edgecloud.com (both ok to be org admins).
- API key: procurement prefers EdgeCloud to generate a scoped key and provide via DocuSign or our secure vault; is that compatible with your onboarding?
- IP allowlist: our infra team will provide static egress ranges by EOD tomorrow. Current expected CIDRs: 3.120.64.0/20 (app agents) and 3.121.0.0/22 (management). These may change if we put the test cluster behind NAT; we’ll flag that in the follow-up.
- VPC peering: we prefer AWS Transit Gateway for the long-term, but we can accept a simple VPC peering for the POC to get started. Our networking contact is Raj Patel (raj.patel@edgecloud.com).

Procurement note: we’re targeting signature on the evaluation SOW by 2027-04-22. If that slips, we’ll still try to run the early environment with a NDA-scoped test account.

I’m attaching a small CSV with VPC metadata (edge_vpc_info.csv).

On the API key process: if you can create a short-lived scoped key and we confirm it’s consumed, we’ll extend access via our vault later. Otherwise we’ll follow your instructions for secure transfer.

Thanks — Lisa
Lisa Montgomery
VP, Cloud Integrations | EdgeCloud Systems
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Montgomery <lisa.montgomery@edgecloud.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Eval environment gating — API keys, org access, IP allowlist, VPC peering

Lisa — perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of concrete next steps from our side:

1) API key approach: we can generate a short-lived scoped API key (read/write for the POC namespace, expires in 14d). We will not persist the key in our console after transfer — if you prefer to post it to your vault, let us know and we’ll provide instructions for ingestion. Attached are the step-by-step instructions we typically send (redwood_temp_key_instructions.md).

2) IP allowlist: once you confirm the final CIDRs, we’ll add them to the allowlist and start the gate tests. Note that if ranges change after we enable them, we’ll need at least a 4-hour maintenance window to update peering rules on the test fleet.

3) VPC peering: Steph and Vivek are on this thread to coordinate. For the POC we can accept a VPC peering connection and then migrate to Transit Gateway in a later MAP step. To move forward we need the following from Raj: VPC ID, region, CIDR, and a preferred peering route table.

4) Canary scope: propose a 2-hour canary window with a synthetic workload (see MAP checklist) to validate stable KV cache behavior and response P95s. If that passes we’ll expand to a 24-hour soak.

If procurement signs the SOW before the 22nd we’ll flip to dedicated capacity; otherwise we’ll stay in shared hosted with IP allowlist + scoped key.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a short 15-minute handoff today between Steph and Raj to confirm the peering parameters.

Best,
Diego

Date: Thu, 14 Apr 2027 14:33:00 -07:00
Subject: ACTION: Peering ticket + temporary key handoff (EdgeCloud POC)

Steph / Vivek — looping you both in to execute the technical steps now that EdgeCloud confirmed org admins and initial CIDRs. Key items below (pulled from thread):

- EdgeCloud contacts: Raj Patel <raj.patel@edgecloud.com> (networking), Lisa Montgomery <lisa.montgomery@edgecloud.com> (integration), Tom Reed <tom.reed@edgecloud.com> (procurement).
- Confirmed provisional CIDRs: 3.120.64.0/20 (agents), 3.121.0.0/22 (management) — final confirmation expected tomorrow.
- VPC peering: create temporary VPC peering conn in us-east-1 between redwood-test-vpc (10.10.0.0/16) and EdgeCloud VPC (CIDR from CSV). Use route table rtb-0a1b2c3d for the redwood side. Please set a short TTL for route propagation while we evaluate.
- API key: I will generate a 14-day scoped API key and not persist it. Plan: generate -> share link to Lisa (DocuSign or vault ingestion) -> invalidate after 14 days.

Please confirm you can pick this up in the next 2 business hours so we can meet the MAP Day 2 objective. If either of you need a quick call with Raj, I can bring him into a 15-min sync.
